inputs.shares_note: Post-split (July 2025 8-for-10 bonus + 12-for-10 capitalisation, ~3.13x pre-split). Pre-split shares FY2024: 2,909.3M
inputs.net_debt_note: Negative = net cash position. Cash 102,257M minus Debt 41,652M. Debt figure from FY2024 balance sheet; note Q3-2025 long-term debt surged 641% to 61.2bn as overseas capex funded via debt
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2024 FCF = Operating CF 133,454M minus CapEx 97,360M. FCF is lumpy due to capex cycles; FY2025 FCF was negative per analyst estimates

historical_growth.growth_rate_note: Historical CAGRs (Revenue 44.9%, EPS 94.3% over 5yr) reflect extraordinary NEV market capture 2019-2024 during EV penetration surge — not forward-replicable at RMB777bn scale. FY2025 revenue grew only 3.5% (guidance-confirmed). Forward base rate anchored on consensus RMB850-900bn for FY2026 (~10-12% growth), fading to terminal 3%. Equity 5yr CAGR (26.7%) used as secondary conservatism check. EPS CAGR wildly distorted by 2019/2021 profit troughs.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (94.3%) diverges 67.6pp from Equity 5yr CAGR (26.7%), exceeding 30pp threshold. Driven by extreme FY2019 EPS trough (RMB0.50) and FY2021 EPS trough (RMB1.06) relative to subsequent recovery. EPS CAGR not used as growth anchor. Revenue CAGR (44.9%) also diverges 18.2pp from Equity CAGR — within tolerance but noted. Forward projections anchored to guidance/consensus rather than backward-looking CAGRs.
historical_growth.fcf_note: FY2024 FCF margin 4.6% (36,094 / 777,103). FCF declined from FY2023 (47,632M) due to capex surge. FY2025 FCF likely negative as investing outflows hit 127.6bn in 9M-2025. Projections use revenue-based FCF margin approach to normalise across capex cycle.

base.growth_rationale: Aligned with FY2026 consensus (~10% revenue growth). Decelerates as domestic market matures; overseas expansion partially offsets. 7% terminal-approach rate reflects large absolute base.
base.fcf_margin_rationale: Modest recovery from FY2024 trough (4.6%) as capex cycle peaks and overseas revenue (higher margin) grows. Below FY2022-23 levels given continued domestic price pressure.
base.wacc_rationale: 11% reflects: risk-free rate ~4% (Chinese 10yr gov bond), equity risk premium ~6%, country risk premium ~1%, beta ~1.1. Higher than typical global auto due to EV price war uncertainty, capex intensity, and geopolitical risk.
base.terminal_growth_rationale: Aligned with long-run Chinese nominal GDP growth expectation. BYD operates globally so slightly above China-only assumption.

bull.growth_rationale: Overseas exports hit 1.5M units in FY2026 as guided (+43% YoY). Hungary factory ramps. BESS shipments grow 50%+ globally. Domestic mix shifts to premium brands (Denza, FANGCHENGBAO) improving ASP. Electronics arm benefits from AI data center hardware demand.
bull.fcf_margin_rationale: Overseas revenue (premium-priced, per management commentary) and reduced capex intensity post-overseas factory buildout. Aligns with FY2022 margins when scale was leveraging fixed costs.
bull.wacc_rationale: Lower risk premium as overseas diversification reduces China concentration risk and EU factory mitigates tariff headwinds.
bull.terminal_growth_rationale: BESS global market leadership (>50% annual industry growth) provides durable long-term growth above GDP.

bear.growth_rationale: Domestic price war persists; China market share declines to 20-22% as Xiaomi/Huawei/Geely accelerate. EU tariff mitigation slower than expected (Hungary ramp delayed). FY2026 starts at -11.8% YoY (Q1 2026 actual); bear assumes this persists through H1 2026.
bear.fcf_margin_rationale: Margin compression from ongoing price cuts, rising R&D (53% YoY in H1-2025) and heavy capex for overseas factories not yet generating returns. Near FY2024 trough with no recovery.
bear.wacc_rationale: Higher risk premium for deteriorating profitability, rising leverage (LT debt +641% by Q3-2025), and geopolitical risk crystallising.
bear.terminal_growth_rationale: Below-GDP growth as commoditised auto market dynamics dominate; Chinese EV brands compete on price rather than value.

sensitivity.note: Base case growth rates [10,10,9,8,7%] and FCF margin 5.5% held constant. Values in HKD.
sensitivity.current_price_marker: WACC=11%, TG=3.0% gives HKD 91.2 — essentially at fair value

probability_weighted.note: Bull 25% / Base 50% / Bear 25% reflects high uncertainty given Q1 2026 profit collapse (-55% YoY) and ongoing domestic price war, offset by credible overseas growth trajectory

key_observations: At HKD 91.60, BYD trades at essentially fair value on the base case (HKD 91.18 IV). The stock has de-rated from HKD 400+ mid-2025 peak.

The base case incorporates modest FCF margin recovery (5.5% vs FY2024's 4.6%). If capex remains elevated through FY2026-27 as overseas factories ramp, FCF margins stay suppressed and base IV falls toward bear territory.

The bull case (HKD 171 IV, +87% upside) requires: overseas exports hitting 1.5M+ units, FCF margins recovering to 7.5%, and WACC remaining at 10%. This is achievable but requires ~3 years of execution without major setbacks.
Q1 2026 result (-55% profit YoY, -11.8% revenue YoY) is a near-term headwind but partly FX-driven (RMB2bn loss) and seasonal. Monitor Q2 2026 closely.

The net cash position (RMB 60.6bn) is significant — it adds approximately HKD 7.25 per post-split share to intrinsic value. However, Q3-2025 showed long-term debt up 641% to 61.2bn, which could erode net cash materially by FY2025 year-end.

At current price, the bull scenario must be assigned meaningful probability to justify buying. The probability-weighted IV of HKD 99.32 implies only +8.4% upside at current price — modest for the risks involved.
Sensitivity table shows current price is only supported at WACC >= 10% with base assumptions. At WACC 9% the stock looks cheap; at WACC 12% it is 17% overvalued even on base assumptions.
